name: Ab Wheel Rollout
cues: Kneel on pad; tuck pelvis into posterior tilt, round upper back slightly, and brace abs hard.
Roll wheel forward under control, extending arms while keeping lower back from sagging.
Roll out only as far as core can maintain the hollow-body braced position.
Pull wheel back by contracting abs and engaging lats, keeping hips forward until reset.
avoid: Allowing lower back to sag into hyperextension (anterior pelvic tilt).
Sitting hips straight back onto heels to pull the wheel in (hip flexor cheat).
Rolling out further than abdominal strength can stabilize.

name: Barbell Back Squat
cues: Set bar firmly on upper traps/shelf; pull bar down into back to engage lats.
Take a 360° diaphragmatic breath into abdomen; break at hips and knees simultaneously.
Descend until hip crease dips below top of knee, knees tracking in line with toes.
Drive through mid-foot with chest and hips rising at the exact same rate.
avoid: Knees caving inward (valgus collapse) on ascent.
Hips shooting up first ('good-morning' squat), shifting load onto lower back.
Rounding or hyperextending lumbar spine at the bottom.

name: Barbell Bench Press
cues: Lie with eyes under bar; plant feet firmly and pin shoulder blades down and back into bench.
Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder-width; unrack and stabilize directly over shoulders.
Lower bar in a slight arc to mid-to-lower sternum, tucking elbows at 45–70°.
Press bar explosively upward and slightly back toward your face, finishing over shoulders.
avoid: Flaring elbows out at 90 degrees to torso (causes subacromial impingement).
Bouncing bar off ribcage or lifting glutes off bench.
Letting wrists bend completely backward under bar.

name: Barbell Front Squat
cues: Rest bar on front deltoids with fingertip clean grip (or cross-arm grip), elbows high and parallel to floor.
Maintain a vertical torso and brace core tightly throughout descent.
Squat between your knees to full comfortable depth, tracking knees forward over toes.
Drive floor away through mid-foot while keeping elbows driven high.
avoid: Elbows dropping downward, causing upper back to round and bar to dump forward.
Heels lifting off floor or weight shifting excessively onto toes.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
cues: Position bench edge just below shoulder blades; rest padded bar across hip crease.
Set feet shoulder-width so shins are strictly vertical (90°) at full extension.
Keep chin tucked to chest and eyes forward; drive through full foot to lift hips.
Squeeze glutes hard into posterior pelvic tilt at top until torso and thighs form a flat table.
avoid: Looking up at the ceiling and hyperextending lumbar spine at the top.
Feet too far forward (hamstrings dominate) or too close (quads dominate).
Letting knees collapse inward during hip extension.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
cues: Stand tall with a shoulder-width grip, lats engaged to keep bar pinned against thighs.
Soften knees slightly and lock that knee angle in place throughout the rep.
Push hips straight back horizontally as if reaching for a wall behind you.
Stop descent once hips stop moving backward (usually mid-shin), then drive hips forward.
avoid: Rounding lower back to reach the floor once hips have stopped traveling back.
Bending knees further into a squat, shifting tension away from hamstrings.
Allowing bar to drift forward away from legs.

name: Barbell Row
cues: Hinge at hips with torso angled at ~45 degrees, lower back flat, knees softly bent.
Take an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, bar hanging over mid-foot.
Drive elbows back behind torso, pulling bar toward lower abdomen / belly button.
Squeeze shoulder blades together at top, then lower bar under control into full stretch.
avoid: Jerking torso upright to heave weight (turning row into a standing shrug).
Rounding lumbar or thoracic spine under load.
Letting shoulders roll forward at the bottom of the rep.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
cues: Place laces of rear foot on bench; step front foot forward into a balanced split stance.
Maintain a slight forward torso lean (~15°) with a braced, neutral spine.
Descend until back knee hovers an inch above the floor, front knee tracking over toes.
Drive straight up through the whole front foot (tripod foot: heel, big toe, pinky toe).
avoid: Front heel lifting off floor or front knee caving inward (valgus collapse).
Pushing aggressively off rear foot instead of loading the front working leg.
Hyperextending lower back by trying to stay unnaturally upright.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
cues: Set pulley at knee or wrist height; stand tall with cable crossing in front or behind body.
Raise arm out and slightly forward in the scapular plane (~30° in front of torso).
Lead with elbow until arm reaches parallel to floor, keeping wrist neutral.
Pause for a split second at peak contraction, then lower under 2–3 second control.
avoid: Swinging torso or using leg bounce to initiate the movement.
Shrugging neck and upper traps up toward ears to lift the cable.
Internally rotating shoulder ('pouring a pitcher of water') during the raise.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
cues: Set bench to a 30–45 degree incline; rest chest firmly against pad with feet planted.
Allow dumbbells to hang straight down at full arm extension, letting shoulder blades stretch open.
Drive elbows back toward hips, retracting shoulder blades firmly at peak contraction.
Lower dumbbells under control into a deep, full back stretch without chest lifting.
avoid: Heaving chest off bench pad to generate momentum.
Craning neck upward toward ceiling.
Pulling with arms/biceps instead of driving through elbows and scapulae.

name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
cues: Set feet hip-width with bar over mid-foot (1 inch from shins); grip just outside legs.
Pull chest tall, engage lats ('protect armpits'), and pull the slack out of the barbell.
Push floor away through mid-foot, keeping bar dragging up shins and thighs.
Stand tall and lock out with glutes; do not lean backward at the top.
avoid: Rounding the lumbar spine under load.
Jerking the barbell off floor without pulling slack first.
Hyperextending lower back at lockout instead of squeezing glutes.
Letting bar drift forward away from legs.

name: Dead Bug
cues: Lie flat on back with arms extended toward ceiling and knees/hips bent at 90 degrees.
Press lower back aggressively flat into floor, eliminating all space under spine.
Slowly extend opposite arm overhead and opposite leg straight toward floor while exhaling fully.
Hover limb 1–2 inches off floor, then return under control while maintaining flat spine.
avoid: Lower back arching or peeling off floor during extension.
Moving limbs rapidly or holding breath.
Letting extended heel slam or rest on floor.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
cues: Retract shoulder blades into bench, plant feet firmly, and hold dumbbells over chest.
Lower dumbbells with control, maintaining vertical forearms and elbows tucked at 45–60°.
Lower into a deep, comfortable chest stretch at bottom without shoulder discomfort.
Press dumbbells up and slightly inward in a smooth arc, stopping just short of touching.
avoid: Clanking dumbbells together at top (removes muscular tension from pecs).
Flaring elbows perpendicular to torso ('T' position).
Allowing forearms to angle inward or outward.

name: Dumbbell Floor Press
cues: Lie flat on floor with knees bent and feet flat; retract shoulder blades into floor.
Hold dumbbells over chest with wrists neutral and elbows tucked at ~45° from torso.
Lower dumbbells under control until upper arms lightly rest flat against floor.
Pause for a split second to remove momentum, then press explosively to full extension.
avoid: Bouncing elbows or triceps hard off the floor.
Flaring elbows wide toward 90 degrees.
Letting wrists collapse backward.

name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
cues: Stand tall holding dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Keep elbows pinned close to ribs; curl dumbbells upward in line with shoulders.
Squeeze brachialis and forearms intensely at top of rep.
Lower dumbbells under strict control to full arm extension without swinging.
avoid: Rocking hips or swinging torso to initiate curl.
Flaring elbows out to sides.
Letting wrists flex or curl inward.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
cues: Stand tall with a slight forward torso hinge (10–15°) and dumbbells at your sides.
Raise dumbbells outward toward walls in the scapular plane (~30° in front of torso).
Lead slightly with elbows until arms are parallel to floor; keep wrists neutral.
Hold peak contraction for a split second, then lower under strict control.
avoid: Shrugging upper traps toward ears to heave the dumbbells up.
Rocking torso back and forth or using hip thrust for momentum.
Internally rotating wrists/shoulders at top (thumbs pointed down).

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
cues: Hold dumbbells against front of thighs with shoulders packed and core braced.
Soften knees and push hips straight back horizontally into a deep hamstring stretch.
Keep dumbbells tracking tightly along thighs and shins.
Reverse movement by driving hips forward once hamstrings are fully lengthened.
avoid: Rounding lumbar spine to chase floor depth.
Letting dumbbells swing forward away from legs.
Squatting the knees forward.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
cues: Hold dumbbells at sides; place entire foot flat on a knee-height box or bench.
Lean torso slightly forward (~10–15°) to center weight over front working leg.
Dorsiflex rear foot (pull toes up) and drive through front foot to stand onto box.
Step down slowly under strict 2–3 second eccentric control without dropping.
avoid: Pushing or springing off the bottom calf/toes to assist ascent.
Letting front knee collapse inward during step-up.
Slamming down onto floor during descent.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
cues: Grip the angled camber of the EZ-bar with palms facing upward and wrists comfortable.
Pin elbows to your sides and brace core; stand tall with knees soft.
Curl bar upward in a smooth arc toward shoulders, squeezing biceps hard at the top.
Lower bar under strict control to full elbow extension without swinging torso.
avoid: Leaning back or hyperextending lumbar spine to heave the weight up.
Swinging elbows far forward to turn curl into a shoulder raise.
Cutting bottom range of motion short before full extension.

name: Face Pull
cues: Set cable pulley to eye level with rope attachment; grip rope with thumbs pointing backward.
Step back into an athletic staggered stance with core braced and ribs pulled down.
Pull center of rope toward forehead while driving elbows high and wide.
Rotate hands back past ears into full external rotation, squeezing rear delts and upper back.
avoid: Craning head and neck forward to meet the rope.
Leaning backward or hyperextending lumbar spine to heave the weight.
Allowing elbows to drop below wrist level (internal rotation fault).

name: Farmer Carry
cues: Deadlift weights to sides with a braced spine; stand tall with chest up and ribs down.
Pack shoulder blades down and back ('anti-shrug') with an intense crush grip.
Walk forward taking short, deliberate, controlled heel-to-toe strides.
Maintain rigid core tension, keeping weights motionless at sides without swinging.
avoid: Waddling or swaying torso side-to-side while walking.
Allowing shoulders to round forward or hyperextending lumbar spine.
Taking long, uncontrolled strides that cause weights to bang against legs.

name: Goblet Squat
cues: Cup hands under top dumbbell head, holding it vertically flush against upper chest.
Set feet slightly wider than shoulder-width, toes turned out 20–30°.
Sit hips down between knees to full depth, letting elbows track inside knees.
Drive through mid-foot to stand, squeezing glutes at the top without hyperextending.
avoid: Letting dumbbell drift forward away from chest (increases spinal moment arm).
Heels lifting off the floor or lower back rounding at the bottom.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
cues: Hang from bar with an overhand grip, engaging shoulders down and back (active hang).
Squeeze legs together; curl pelvis upward toward chest as knees rise.
Pause for 1 second at top contraction with knees at chest level.
Lower knees under control to a dead stop before starting next rep.
avoid: Swinging legs or using hip momentum to kick knees up.
Arching lower back at the bottom of the rep.
Hanging passively with relaxed shoulders shrugged to ears.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
cues: Set bench to 30 degrees; plant feet firmly and pin shoulder blades into pad.
Grip slightly wider than shoulder width; unrack bar directly over upper chest.
Lower under control to upper chest/sternum (just below collarbones) with elbows at ~45–60°.
Press bar up and slightly back to full extension over upper chest.
avoid: Bouncing bar off collarbones or ribcage.
Flaring elbows out wide to 90 degrees.
Arching lower back excessively (which flattens the torso and eliminates incline angle).

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
cues: Set bench to 55–60 degrees; sit back with head and torso supported by pad.
Let arms hang straight down toward floor, keeping upper arms strictly vertical.
Curl dumbbells upward, supinating wrists (palms up) as you ascend into a hard bicep peak.
Lower under strict 2–3 second control into a deep, full stretch at the bottom.
avoid: Swinging upper arms or elbows forward to bypass the bottom stretch.
Lifting head or shoulders off bench pad during the curl.
Cutting the eccentric stretch short.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
cues: Set bench to 30 degrees; retract shoulder blades and plant feet firmly on floor.
Lower dumbbells under control to sides of upper chest, elbows angled at 45–60°.
Feel a deep stretch across upper pectorals at the bottom with forearms vertical.
Press dumbbells up and slightly inward over upper chest without clanking them together.
avoid: Arching lower back excessively to turn the press into a flat bench press.
Flaring elbows perpendicular to torso.
Banging dumbbells together at top of rep.

name: Jump Rope
cues: Keep elbows pinned close to ribs, turning the rope primarily with relaxed wrists.
Jump lightly on balls of feet, clearing floor by only 1–2 inches per rotation.
Maintain soft knees and ankles to absorb impact with natural elastic rebound.
Keep breathing relaxed, rhythm steady, and torso tall.
avoid: Swinging whole arms from shoulder joints instead of turning with wrists.
Jumping excessively high or kicking feet backward (donkey kicks).
Landing stiff-legged or flat on heels.

name: Kettlebell Swing
cues: Stand 1 foot behind bell; hike bell backward high between inner thighs like a football snap.
Drive hips forward explosively, snapping hips to standing with glutes and abs clenched.
Let kettlebell float to chest height purely from hip momentum; keep arms relaxed like ropes.
Let bell free-fall back into the hinge, waiting until forearms connect with inner thighs to hinge.
avoid: Squatting the knees forward instead of hinging hips back.
Actively lifting the bell with anterior deltoids and arms.
Leaning back and hyperextending lumbar spine at top of swing.

name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
cues: Kneel facing cable; glue rope handles to sides of forehead/ears with hands fixed.
Keep hips high and stationary throughout; do not let hips sit back toward heels.
Flex spine to curl ribcage down toward pelvis, pulling elbows toward upper thighs.
Squeeze abs hard at peak contraction, then resist cable back into a full torso extension.
avoid: Sitting hips back onto heels during crunch (shifts load to hip flexors).
Pulling rope with arms or lats instead of flexing spine with abs.
Keeping spine straight and hinging at hips.

name: Lat Pulldown
cues: Adjust thigh pads securely over legs; grip bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Lean torso back slightly (10–15 degrees) with chest proud and shoulder blades depressed.
Drive elbows straight down toward your front hip pockets, pulling bar to upper chest.
Squeeze lats at bottom, then control bar up into a full overhead stretch.
avoid: Leaning back excessively (turning the pulldown into a sloppy horizontal row).
Driving elbows far behind torso instead of pulling down in front.
Pulling bar behind neck or yanking down to stomach.

name: Leg Extension
cues: Align machine pivot point directly with your knee joints; adjust shin pad just above ankles.
Grip side handles firmly to lock hips and pelvis down into the seat throughout the set.
Extend knees smoothly and hold a peak quad squeeze for 1 full second at top.
Lower under strict 2–3 second eccentric control through full range of motion.
avoid: Hips lifting off the seat pad or using torso momentum to kick the weight up.
Letting the weight stack slam between reps.

name: Leg Press
cues: Place feet shoulder-width on center of platform, knees in line with toes.
Pull seat handles firmly to anchor your hips and lower back flat against back pad.
Lower sled under control as deep as hip mobility allows without pelvis curling off pad.
Press platform away through mid-foot, stopping just short of a harsh knee lockout.
avoid: Pelvis tucking under or lower back rounding off the back pad ('butt wink').
Forcefully hyperextending or snapping knee joints locked at the top.
Knees caving inward during the descent or initial press.

name: Lying Leg Curl
cues: Align knee joints with machine pivot point; position pad on lower calf just above Achilles.
Grip handles firmly to pull your hips and pelvis flat into the bench.
Curl heels toward glutes in a smooth arc, holding a brief contraction at peak.
Lower under strict 2–3 second control into full knee extension without slamming stack.
avoid: Hips popping off bench pad or arching lower back to heave weight.
Using ballistic momentum or kicking weights up quickly.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
cues: Place same-side knee and hand firmly on flat bench; keep spine flat and hips square to floor.
Let dumbbell hang directly below shoulder, feeling a full lat stretch at bottom.
Pull dumbbell back toward hip crease in a sweeping arc, driving elbow toward ceiling.
Squeeze lat at top, then lower dumbbell under control into full extension.
avoid: Twisting or rotating torso at the top of the pull to heave the weight.
Rounding lower back during the stretch phase.
Pulling straight up to chest like a bicep curl rather than arcing back to hip.

name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
cues: Set pulley at head/shoulder height; face away in a stable staggered split stance.
Position upper arms alongside ears and forward (~45°), keeping elbows fixed in place.
Extend forearms forward in a straight line until elbows are fully locked out.
Bend elbows under control, letting rope travel behind head into a deep long-head stretch.
avoid: Hyperextending lower back to assist the press (keep ribs down and core braced).
Flaring elbows excessively wide outward during extension.
Moving upper arms back and forth instead of pivoting strictly at elbow joint.

name: Pallof Press
cues: Stand perpendicular to cable in an athletic shoulder-width stance, knees slightly bent.
Hold handle with both hands tight against center of chest, core braced and ribs down.
Press handle straight forward until arms are fully extended, resisting all rotational pull.
Hold at full extension for 2 seconds, then return hands slowly to chest.
avoid: Allowing torso, shoulders, or hips to rotate toward the pulley.
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears during the press.
Rushing through reps without pausing at full extension.

name: Pec Deck Fly
cues: Adjust seat height so handles align with mid-chest; plant feet firmly on floor.
Set a slight, fixed bend in elbows (~15°) and keep chest proud against back pad.
Bring handles together in a wide hugging arc, focusing on squeezing inner biceps together over sternum.
Return under control to a deep pectoral stretch, stopping before shoulders roll forward.
avoid: Letting elbows travel too far behind torso, hyperextending anterior shoulder capsule.
Shrugging upper traps or rolling shoulders forward at peak contraction.
Bending elbows excessively to turn the fly into a chest press.

name: Pull-Ups
cues: Hang with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders in a full dead hang.
Initiate pull by depressing shoulder blades down and back ('pull shoulders into back pockets').
Drive elbows down toward floor, pulling upper chest toward bar until chin clears bar.
Lower under strict control back into a full dead hang before starting next rep.
avoid: Kipping, swinging legs, or using hip momentum to clear the bar.
Craning neck upward to touch bar while chest collapses.
Performing half reps by failing to lock out into a dead hang at bottom.

name: Weighted Pull-Ups
cues: Secure the plate to a dipping belt and let it hang between your legs.
Start in a full hang with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your elbows down until your chin clears the fixed bar.
Lower under control to straight arms, keeping the plate still.
avoid: Swinging the plate or using hip momentum to pull up.
Using an unsecured belt, chain, or plate.
Shortening the range of motion as the load increases.

name: Push Press
cues: Set bar in front rack across shoulders, hands just outside shoulders, core braced.
Dip knees 3–4 inches vertically, keeping torso strictly upright (do not hinge forward).
Explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles to drive the bar off shoulders.
Finish the press overhead with arms locked firmly out over mid-foot.
avoid: Leaning torso forward during the dip (causes bar to travel forward).
Dipping too deep or too slowly, losing the elastic stretch-shortening reflex.
Re-bending knees to catch the bar (push press requires catching with straight legs).

name: Push-Ups
cues: Set hands slightly wider than shoulder width; create a rigid plank from head to heels.
Lower body as a single unit until chest touches or hovers 1 inch above floor.
Keep elbows tucked at roughly 45 degrees (forming an arrowhead, not a 'T').
Press floor away to full arm extension, actively spreading shoulder blades apart at the top.
avoid: Sagging hips into lumbar hyperextension or piking hips into the air.
Flaring elbows straight out to sides (shoulder impingement risk).
Craning neck down to touch floor before chest.

name: Rope Triceps Pressdown
cues: Stand tall with a slight forward torso lean; pin elbows firmly against sides of ribcage.
Grip rope with neutral hands; press straight down until elbows are fully extended.
Spread rope ends apart at full lockout, squeezing triceps hard for 1 second.
Allow forearms to rise past 90 degrees toward chest under control for a deep triceps stretch.
avoid: Cutting off the eccentric stretch by stopping artificially at 90 degrees elbow flexion.
Allowing elbows to swing forward and backward during the rep.
Leaning bodyweight down on top of rope to push with chest and shoulders.

name: Seated Leg Curl
cues: Adjust backrest so knee joints align with machine pivot; lock thigh pad tightly over lower quads.
Position ankle pad against lower calves/Achilles; keep toes neutral or slightly dorsiflexed.
Drive heels down and back underneath seat into full knee flexion, pausing for 1 second.
Resist the return under control, feeling a deep stretch at full knee extension.
avoid: Loose thigh pad allowing thighs or hips to lift during curl.
Cutting range of motion short at either top stretch or bottom flexion.
Leaning torso far back during the pull.

name: Seated Machine Calf Raise
cues: Sit with balls of feet on platform; adjust thigh pad firmly over lower quads (above knees).
Lower heels down into a deep calf stretch; hold the bottom stretch for 2 full seconds.
Press platform away through balls of feet into full plantarflexion.
Squeeze soleus hard at peak height for 1 second before controlling descent.
avoid: Bouncing off Achilles tendon at the bottom of the rep.
Cutting range of motion into short, twitchy half-reps.
Setting thigh pad too high up on mid-thighs, causing instability.

name: Side Plank
cues: Lie on side with elbow directly beneath shoulder, forearms flat, feet stacked or staggered.
Lift hips off floor to create a straight, unbroken diagonal line from head to heels.
Keep shoulders and hips square (stacked vertically), bracing obliques and glutes.
Maintain steady breathing and keep head aligned with spine.
avoid: Hips sagging toward floor or piking backward.
Rotating chest and shoulders forward toward floor.
Shrugging supporting shoulder up toward ear.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
cues: Place ball of working foot on edge of step; lightly hold wall or rack with one hand for balance.
Keep working leg straight (micro-soft knee) and let non-working leg hang freely.
Lower heel below step level into a deep calf stretch; pause for 2 full seconds.
Drive forcefully through big toe to full height, squeezing calf hard at the top.
avoid: Bouncing rapidly at the bottom without pausing.
Bending working knee to spring body upward.
Rolling ankle outward onto pinky toe at peak height.

name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
cues: Grip bar just outside shoulders; rest bar on front delts with forearms vertical and elbows slightly forward.
Squeeze glutes, quads, and abs to create an immovable base.
Pull chin back slightly to clear bar path; press bar in a straight vertical line overhead.
Push head forward once bar clears forehead; lock out bar directly over mid-foot with a slight trap shrug.
avoid: Arching lower back excessively (leaning back to turn it into an incline press).
Dipping knees to initiate press (this is a strict press, not a push press).
Pressing bar in a wide, looping forward arc around head.

name: Standing Machine Calf Raise
cues: Place balls of feet on edge of block, shoulder-width; keep knees straight with a micro-bend.
Lower heels as deep as ankle mobility allows; hold a full 2-second stretch at the bottom.
Drive up forcefully through the balls of feet, focusing pressure through the big toes.
Squeeze calves hard at peak contraction for 1 second before descending.
avoid: Bouncing out of bottom stretch (relies on Achilles tendon elasticity instead of muscle).
Bending and extending knees to heave weight up (turning it into a squat).
Rolling ankles outward onto pinky toes.

name: Straight Bar Cable Triceps Pressdown
cues: Take an overhand grip on straight bar with hands shoulder-width apart.
Pin elbows firmly to sides of torso and maintain a slight athletic forward hinge.
Push bar straight down to full elbow extension, squeezing triceps at lockout.
Control bar back up past 90 degrees to upper chest level for a complete stretch.
avoid: Letting shoulders round forward or using chest weight to force the bar down.
Elbows drifting forward on the way down or swinging with momentum.
Excessive wrist flexion (curling wrists down).

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
cues: Stand centered between handles with feet hip-to-shoulder-width; grip center of handles.
Drop hips into a hybrid hinge-squat, chest proud, lats engaged to set spine neutral.
Drive the floor away through mid-foot with explosive intent.
Stand tall to full hip and knee lockout, squeezing glutes at the top.
avoid: Rounding lower back during the initial break off the floor.
Starting with hips too high (stiff-legging) or too low (shoving knees into handles).
Shrugging shoulders or hyperextending spine at lockout.

name: Cable Seated Row
cues: Establish stable posture with chest upright and core braced tight.
Initiate pull by retracting shoulder blades and driving elbows straight back.
Pull handle or bar toward lower abdomen / waistline, contracting mid-back and lats.
Control the return into a deep stretch without letting shoulders collapse forward.
avoid: Using excessive torso swing or leg drive to jerk the weight.
Rounding upper or lower spine under load.
Flaring elbows excessively wide away from body.

name: Dumbbell Seated Shoulder Press
cues: Set stable base with ribs pulled down, core braced, and glutes engaged.
Position weight at shoulder height with elbows stacked directly under wrists.
Press weight straight upward, clearing head and finishing in line with ears.
Lower under control back to collarbone level without losing core tightness.
avoid: Arching lower back excessively to compensate for shoulder mobility.
Flaring elbows out completely wide to the sides.
Using leg drive on strict pressing variations.

name: Lever Chest Press
cues: Retract and depress shoulder blades firmly into bench; establish solid foot drive.
Unrack weight over shoulders; lower smoothly with elbows tucked at 45–70°.
Descend until dumbbells/bar reach chest level under full muscular control.
Press up and slightly back toward shoulder line, contracting chest forcefully.
avoid: Flaring elbows out at 90 degrees to torso (causes shoulder impingement).
Bouncing bar off ribcage or lifting glutes off the bench.
Losing upper back tightness at the top of the press.

name: Lever Seated Shoulder Press
cues: Set stable base with ribs pulled down, core braced, and glutes engaged.
Position weight at shoulder height with elbows stacked directly under wrists.
Press weight straight upward, clearing head and finishing in line with ears.
Lower under control back to collarbone level without losing core tightness.
avoid: Arching lower back excessively to compensate for shoulder mobility.
Flaring elbows out completely wide to the sides.
Using leg drive on strict pressing variations.

name: Bodyweight Rear Lunge
cues: Adopt a stable staggered stance with hips square and core braced tight.
Lower straight down until back knee hovers an inch above floor and front thigh is parallel.
Maintain a slight forward torso lean (~10°) aligned with front shin.
Drive forcefully through front heel and mid-foot to rise back to starting lockout.
avoid: Banging back knee hard into the floor.
Letting front heel lift or front knee collapse inward.
Arching lower back excessively by forcing a vertical spine.

name: Walking Lunge
cues: Adopt a stable staggered stance with hips square and core braced tight.
Lower straight down until back knee hovers an inch above floor and front thigh is parallel.
Maintain a slight forward torso lean (~10°) aligned with front shin.
Drive forcefully through front heel and mid-foot to rise back to starting lockout.
avoid: Banging back knee hard into the floor.
Letting front heel lift or front knee collapse inward.
Arching lower back excessively by forcing a vertical spine.

name: Bodyweight Squat
cues: Set stable stance with feet shoulder-width, toes angled slightly out; brace core.
Initiate descent by breaking at hips and knees together, keeping chest proud.
Descend until hip crease is at or below top of knee while keeping whole foot planted.
Drive evenly through mid-foot and heels to ascend with hips and chest rising in unison.
avoid: Knees caving inward (valgus collapse) on the ascent.
Hips shooting up first ('good-morning' squat), shifting load to lumbar spine.
Heels lifting or excessive forward torso collapse.

name: Lever Seated Reverse Fly
cues: Hinge forward at hips with flat back (or lay chest-down on incline bench).
With slight elbow bend, sweep arms out wide in the transverse plane.
Squeeze rear deltoids firmly at top without shrugging traps toward neck.
Lower weights under controlled eccentric tempo, maintaining tension.
avoid: Swinging torso upward to use momentum.
Turning rear fly into a lat row by pulling elbows down.

name: Cable Curl
cues: Stand tall with elbows pinned at sides and shoulders pulled back.
Curl weight upward by flexing biceps, keeping upper arms completely stationary.
Squeeze biceps hard at the peak, supinating wrists if using dumbbells.
Lower the weight under slow 2–3 second control into full elbow extension.
avoid: Swinging elbows forward or backward to generate momentum.
Arching lower back to lean backward during the curl.

name: Barbell Preacher Curl
cues: Position upper arms firmly flat against pad with armpits wedged at the top edge.
Keep wrists firm; curl weight upward by flexing biceps while keeping triceps glued to pad.
Squeeze biceps hard at peak contraction without lifting elbows off pad.
Lower weight under strict 2–3 second control until arms are nearly fully extended.
avoid: Hyperextending and bouncing violently off the bottom elbow lockout.
Lifting elbows or leaning back off the pad during the curl.

name: Chest Dip
cues: Grasp bars with arms locked; lean torso forward ~20–30° to target chest.
Lower body under control by bending elbows until upper arms are parallel to floor.
Keep elbows tucked at ~45° rather than flared wide.
Press through palms and contract lower pecs to return to lockout.
avoid: Descending too deep past comfort, placing excessive strain on anterior shoulder capsule.
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears during descent.

name: Chin-up

Press forcefully through big toes to elevate heels into maximal plantarflexion.
Hold peak contraction for a split second before controlling the descent.
avoid: Bending and extending knees to turn calf raise into a mini squat.
Rushing reps and cutting the bottom stretch or top squeeze.

name: Sissy Squat Bodyweight
cues: Stand tall with feet hip-width; hold a stable upright for balance if needed.
Drive knees forward and down while leaning torso back in a straight line from knees to head.
Descend until shins and thighs form a deep angle, loading the rectus femoris.
Drive through balls of feet and contract quadriceps forcefully to return upright.
avoid: Bending at the hips (breaking neutral hip alignment).
Dropping into knee flexion without muscular quadriceps control.

name: Sled Reverse Hack Squat
cues: Sit with back and hips firmly against pad, feet shoulder-width on footplate.
Release safety catches; lower sled smoothly until knees reach ~90° without butt lifting.
Keep knees tracking in line with second toes throughout the descent.
Press through mid-foot and heels to return to start, stopping just short of knee lockout.
avoid: Allowing pelvis to tuck or lower back to round off backrest at bottom (butt wink).
Locking knees out violently into hyperextension under heavy load.

name: Heel-Elevated Bodyweight Squat
cues: Set stable stance with feet shoulder-width, toes angled slightly out; brace core.
Initiate descent by breaking at hips and knees together, keeping chest proud.
Descend until hip crease is at or below top of knee while keeping whole foot planted.
Drive evenly through mid-foot and heels to ascend with hips and chest rising in unison.
avoid: Knees caving inward (valgus collapse) on the ascent.
Hips shooting up first ('good-morning' squat), shifting load to lumbar spine.
Heels lifting or excessive forward torso collapse.

name: Cossack Squat
cues: Take an extra-wide stance with toes pointing forward or slightly outward; brace core.
Shift weight to working side, sitting hip back and down while keeping opposite leg straight.
Descend until working hip crease is deep, keeping working heel planted firmly.
Drive through working mid-foot to push back to the tall starting position.
avoid: Allowing working heel to lift off the floor during the descent.
Rounding lumbar spine or collapsing chest forward under load.

name: Dumbbell Curtsey Lunge
cues: Stand tall holding weights; step one leg diagonally back behind front leg.
Descend by bending both knees until front thigh is parallel and back knee hovers off floor.
Keep chest upright, hips facing mostly forward, and front foot planted solid.
Drive through front heel and glute to step back to the center starting position.
avoid: Rotating pelvis excessively away from the forward plane.
Letting front knee cave inward past big toe.

name: Dumbbell Deficit Reverse Lunge
cues: Adopt a stable staggered stance with hips square and core braced tight.
Lower straight down until back knee hovers an inch above floor and front thigh is parallel.
Maintain a slight forward torso lean (~10°) aligned with front shin.
Drive forcefully through front heel and mid-foot to rise back to starting lockout.
avoid: Banging back knee hard into the floor.
Letting front heel lift or front knee collapse inward.
Arching lower back excessively by forcing a vertical spine.

Drive down through lead heel and mid-foot to elevate body without springing off trailing foot.
Reach full hip extension at top on working leg, squeezing glute.
Lower trailing foot back down under 2-second control, keeping tension on front leg.
avoid: Pushing aggressively off rear toe instead of pulling with lead leg.
Allowing lead knee to cave inward or lead heel to hang off platform.

name: Lever Standing Single-Leg Curl

Dorsiflex ankles slightly; contract hamstrings forcefully to curl heels toward glutes.
Pause for a full second at peak knee flexion, squeezing hamstrings completely.
Lower weight under strict 2–3 second control until legs are nearly straight.
avoid: Arching lower back or lifting hips off pad to throw momentum into the curl.
Allowing weight stack to slam down on the eccentric return.

name: Bodyweight Frog Hip Thrust
cues: Position upper back across bench just below shoulder blades; place feet flat shoulder-width.
Tuck chin slightly and engage core; drive through heels to elevate hips toward the ceiling.
Reach full hip extension where thighs and torso form a flat tabletop, squeezing glutes hard.
Lower hips back down with control, keeping ribs pulled down and chin tucked.
avoid: Hyperextending lumbar spine at top instead of achieving true hip extension.
Pushing through toes rather than driving into heels.
Letting knees collapse inward during hip drive.

cues: Set stable torso position; brace core to prevent lumbar hyperextension.
Drive working leg back/out using isolated glute contraction without rotating hips.
Hold peak contraction for a split second to maximize glute activation.
Return leg smoothly under control to starting alignment.
avoid: Arching lower back to kick leg higher.
Twisting pelvis or swinging leg with momentum.

name: Reverse Hyperextension on Box
cues: Position thighs securely against pads with hip crease just above edge for free hip flexion.
Brace core with neutral spine; hinge forward at hips until hamstrings are fully stretched.
Contract glutes and hamstrings to pull torso back in line with legs; hold for a count.
Keep spine neutral rather than arching past straight alignment.
avoid: Hyperextending lumbar spine excessively at the top of the extension.
Jerking torso upward with swinging momentum.

name: Handstand Push-up
cues: Retract and depress shoulder blades firmly into bench; establish solid foot drive.
Unrack weight over shoulders; lower smoothly with elbows tucked at 45–70°.
Descend until dumbbells/bar reach chest level under full muscular control.
Press up and slightly back toward shoulder line, contracting chest forcefully.
avoid: Flaring elbows out at 90 degrees to torso (causes shoulder impingement).
Bouncing bar off ribcage or lifting glutes off the bench.
Losing upper back tightness at the top of the press.

name: Ring Dip
cues: Pin elbows firmly at sides and lean torso forward slightly with braced core.
Extend forearms down by contracting triceps until arms are fully straight.
Squeeze triceps hard at bottom lockout, spreading ropes or gripping bar firm.
Return weight under 2-second control to ~90° elbow bend, keeping elbows pinned.
avoid: Allowing elbows to drift forward and backward on each rep.
Using shoulder or torso momentum to slam weight down.

name: Resistance Band Seated Row

Initiate pull by retracting shoulder blades and driving elbows straight back.
Pull handle or bar toward lower abdomen / waistline, contracting mid-back and lats.
Control the return into a deep stretch without letting shoulders collapse forward.
avoid: Using excessive torso swing or leg drive to jerk the weight.
Rounding upper or lower spine under load.
Flaring elbows excessively wide away from body.

name: Resistance Band Lat Pulldown
cues: Grasp bar with chosen grip; secure thighs under pads and lift chest.
Initiate by pulling shoulder blades down and driving elbows down and back toward ribs.
Pull bar smoothly to upper chest / chin level while keeping spine tall.
Control the eccentric return under full lat stretch, allowing scapulae to elevate.
avoid: Leaning back excessively into a horizontal row to heave the weight.
Pulling bar behind the neck (strains cervical spine and rotator cuff).
Using jerky momentum to yank the bar down.

Curl weight upward by flexing biceps, keeping upper arms completely stationary.
Squeeze biceps hard at the peak, supinating wrists if using dumbbells.
Lower the weight under slow 2–3 second control into full elbow extension.
avoid: Swinging elbows forward or backward to generate momentum.
Arching lower back to lean backward during the curl.

name: Resistance Band Triceps Pushdown

name: Band Lateral Raise
cues: Lean torso forward ~10–15° with soft knees and core braced.
Raise arms out in scapular plane (~30° forward), leading with elbows.
Stop when hands reach shoulder height, keeping pinkies slightly above thumbs.
Control the descent slowly, keeping constant tension on lateral delts.
avoid: Shrugging neck and upper traps up toward ears.
Swinging torso or bouncing knees to heave the weights.
Internally rotating shoulders excessively during the raise.

name: Landmine 180
cues: Stand in athletic stance with core braced; hold handle/bar with both hands.
Rotate torso diagonally across body by driving from the obliques and hips.
Pivot on back foot smoothly while keeping arms mostly extended.
Control the return path against cable/weight resistance, resisting rotation.
avoid: Bending arms and pulling purely with shoulders/arms.
Twisting spine without pivoting trailing foot, stressing lower back.

name: Hanging Toes to Bar
cues: Flatten lower back into the floor or maintain stable braced spine.
Contract abdominals to curl ribs toward hips, expelling air forcefully.
Hold peak contraction for a count, focusing purely on abdominal flexion.
Lower under control, keeping tension on abs without resting completely.
avoid: Yanking on neck with hands or throwing head forward.
Using hip flexor momentum to swing legs or torso.

name: Battling Ropes High Waves
cues: Adopt an athletic half-squat stance with chest proud and core braced.
Grip rope ends firmly; generate rapid alternating or simultaneous waves from shoulders.
Keep torso rigid and absorb energy through hips and legs, not lower back.
Breathe rhythmically while sustaining maximum wave velocity.
avoid: Standing completely upright and letting ropes pull torso forward.
Rounding upper back into a hunched posture.

name: Power Sled Push
cues: Grip sled poles firmly with arms extended or forearms on bars; lean torso forward at 45°.
Brace core and drive aggressively through balls of feet with deep knee drive.
Maintain a rigid neutral spine from head to heels throughout the push.
Take powerful, marching steps, keeping constant forward momentum.
avoid: Rounding lower back or letting hips sway wildly side to side.
Taking tiny stutter steps that lose ground drive.
